title: Serve plans over HTTP and keep them in SQLite

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny season matches the expected report

blueprint.contract: Returns a FastAPI app whose plans are kept in a Store on the SQLite file db. store.py is new: Store(path) opens one connection (check_same_thread=False, shared under a threading.Lock) and creates the table plans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, input_sha256 TEXT, record TEXT), the record stored as dumps writes it; save(record) -> int inserts a row and returns its id; get(plan_id) -> dict | None returns the stored record parsed back with json.loads, or None for an id with no row. The request is checked by pydantic models in api.py: Span = tuple[int, int]; CircuitIn with id and region (str), miles (int, > 0), cost and risk (int, >= 0), weeks (int, >= 1), growth (float, >= 0), windows (list[Span], default []) and must (bool, default False); SeasonIn with name (default 'season'), budget (int, >= 0), crews (int, 1 to 50), months (int, 1 to 12), crew_off (dict[str, list[Span]], default {}) and circuits (list[CircuitIn], at least one); OverrideIn with kind (pin, skip or force), cid, crew (default None), start (default None) and reason (default ''); PlanRequest with season (SeasonIn) and overrides (list[OverrideIn], default []). POST /plans takes a PlanRequest; it answers 422 with the list of problems when check_overrides finds any, else plans the season (from the validated season's model_dump()) and answers {'id', 'record'}, an infeasible season included. GET /plans/`<id>` answers the same body, or 404 with `no plan <id>`.
blueprint.idea: Validate at the edge, keep the service a thin layer over the library, and store every answer so it outlives the process.

cases: posting a season returns the record the library gives
a stored plan comes back by its id, and an unknown id is 404
an override that names no circuit is refused with 422 and its problem
an infeasible season is an answer, with its explanation
a season with a negative budget is refused with 422, naming the budget
a plan saved by one app comes back from a new app on the same SQLite file
